difference: the pinned mutation-test runner: its docker run argv is built at run time and its networks are configurable: --network for every mutant and diagnostic run (default none; read at :2538, passed at :1298) and --node-seed-network for the one install container of --node-seed-build (TXE-8348; default bridge; read at :2586, passed at :2414, through the same argv builder). The build writes its seed relative to a descriptor, never by pathname (TXE-8385; write_seed, :2264). It refuses to run as root and screens the parent and every ancestor up to / by owner uid, POSIX mode bits and the sticky bit (check_seed_parent, :2321), and the device and inode of that screened lstat are the identity the build requires when it opens the parent O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW (open_seed_parent, :2116). It creates the seed directory with mkdirat at mode 0700 (make_seed_dir, :2142), opens it O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, and refuses the descriptor unless it is the directory at that name now (fstat against an lstat of the name), owned by the invoker, of mode exactly 0700 and empty (open_seed_dir, :2147); that does not prove it is the inode mkdirat created. Every later write is relative to that descriptor (mkdirat, files opened O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, symlinkat), so once it is obtained, a rename of the seed directory or of any ancestor cannot move the writes elsewhere. Prerequisite, not checked: from the screening through the create and the open, no untrusted party can rename or create entries in the parent or replace it through an ancestor; ACLs and other non-mode permissions are not examined, and a process of the invoker's uid is trusted. After the build, a party with ACL or other non-mode write or delete rights on the parent can delete or replace the finished seed directory. The export's equivalence to the earlier copytree export is shown on a real seed's node_modules copied both ways (partial evidence: no rebuild). That container runs the runner's fixed NODE_SEED_SCRIPT (:1512) over the workspace's manifests only, after check_node_config refuses any pnpm configuration outside a closed set, with every lifecycle script disabled; but an optional --node-seed-allow-build list makes the networked pnpm rebuild in it run those packages' install scripts, which can download code and execute it inside the container. Node containers launch by the image's resolved immutable id (:1309). --ro-mount adds one read-only bind of a runner-made copy at /work/src/.git (TXE-8053, appended at :1269). The time, output and disk bounds are monitored and cooperative (watch_run, :1408, polls them and stops a run once it sees one passed), not hard quotas; memory, CPU and process counts are docker's limits. So it is not a fixed reviewed argv and is NOT checked against the argv_guard floor
